newsitem.title: UK: TI's Dowty aerospace unit ready for takeoff.
newsitem.headline: TI's Dowty aerospace unit ready for takeoff.

text.p: TI Group Plc's Dowty aerospace components division said on Wednesday its financial performance would get a lift from the current revival in fortunes for the aircraft industry.

Dowty chief and TI director Tony Edwards said there was a 29 percent growth in underlying operating profits on a nine percent rise in sales last year, reflecting the start of the industry's recovery as airlines take delivery of more new aircraft.
"It's good to be out of recession at last," he told Reuters.
There was already a rise in demand for Dowty Aerospace components from Boeing Co last year as it began increasing production.

But the pick-up in output by Anglo-French landing gear joint venture Messier-Dowty's big customer, Airbus Industrie, was only due to get going in 1997 and this should boost margins further as production capacity is taken up, he said.
"Airbus is coming through a little later so the product mix (from Airbus) was not so good last year for Messier-Dowty," he said.

He later told a results news conference that Dowty was a major supplier of new aircraft components to Boeing, earning about $300,000 in sales from every B-737 built and over $700,000 from every B-777, and Boeing's production increases were "galloping ahead."
But he said the Airbus potential was also huge with Dowty earning $750,000 from an Airbus A320 and $2 million on Airbus A340/A330 widebodies.

"What's driving us is our shipset values," he said. Earlier TI reported a 26 percent rise in group pretax profits to 232.2 million stg last year, with underlying profits before an exceptional gain from disposals up 16 percent at 211.1 million stg.
Sales rose to 1,757 million stg from 1,703 million stg in 1995, with underlying sales growth up eight percent after adjusting for acquisitions and disposals.

Dowty made an operating profit of 44 million stg on sales of 446 million stg while the John Crane mechanical seals and engineering polymers division made an operating profit of 97.1 million stg on sales of 593 million stg.
Bundy, making specialist tubing for refrigeration and vehicle fuel and brake systems, made operating profits of 79.2 million stg on sales of 718 million stg.
